system:
You grade one change in an experiment. You are given the change request, the problem the
researcher seeded in it (the answer key: `none`, or a conflict or breakage and what it is against),
the elements the request is bound to, the edit an arm made, and that arm's pre-deploy findings.

Label every finding, by its number:
- `seeded`: it identifies the seeded problem (the same conflict or breakage, in any words)
- `other-real`: it is a real problem with this change, but not the seeded one
- `false-alarm`: it is not a real problem

Then judge the edit: did it implement the request (`implements`), only part of it (`partial`), or
not at all (`does-not`)? Judge only whether it does what was asked, not whether that is wise.

Reply with JSON only:
{"findings": [{"index": 0, "label": "seeded | other-real | false-alarm", "why": "one sentence"}],
 "edit_fidelity": "implements | partial | does-not", "edit_why": "one sentence"}

0. {"problem": "auto_deploy lets the system deploy with no person involved. The existing deploy action says 'Only a person deploys' and has requires: human and records_decision: true. The glossary's deploy floor lists 'a person deploys' as a rule no declaration can weaken. auto_deploy has actor system, no requires: human and no records_decision. It calls the same kernel deploy, so the kernel floor would refuse it every time, or else the floor is weakened. Either way this contradicts the existing rule.", "where": "delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, actions.auto_deploy vs actions.deploy and glossary 'deploy floor'", "kind": "contradiction"}
1. {"problem": "auto_deploy passes approver: target.approver. That is the person who approved the commit in Authoring, not someone who chose to deploy. The deployment is recorded under that name although they did not trigger it, which gives a false decision trail. deploy uses actor.id, the person actually deploying.", "where": "delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, actions.auto_deploy.effects[0].with.approver", "kind": "other"}
2. {"problem": "The only guard is harness_ok == true, which can be stale. From 'done' (for example R3, harness_ok true), preview moves the request back to 'built' without clearing harness_ok. auto_deploy is then allowed in 'built' before the new build's result is recorded. It would deploy a build whose harness has not run. A person pressing deploy can judge this; an automatic deploy cannot. There is also no guard against redeploying from 'done' when deployed is already true, so it can repeat.", "where": "delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, actions.auto_deploy.preconditions and transitions DeliveryRequest built/done auto_deploy", "kind": "behaviour"}
3. {"problem": "Nothing triggers auto_deploy after a passing preview. There is no handoff, no reply or event on record_build, and no wiring in the composition. The system actor never fires it, so the stated goal of deploying without anyone pressing deploy is not met. There is also no scenario covering auto_deploy.", "where": "delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, actions.auto_deploy / record_build; toprope-self.composition.yaml wiring", "kind": "other"}
4. {"problem": "Other text that describes how deploys work was not updated. The glossary's 'deploy floor' still says a person deploys. The deploy description says 'Only a person deploys'. The scenarios cover only the manual path. These now disagree with the existence of an automatic path.", "where": "delivery/delivery.domain.yaml, glossary.deploy floor, actions.deploy.description, scenarios", "kind": "reference"}
